import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.27

by A. V. Kuznetsov

Does the lattice of all varieties of groups possess non-trivial automorphisms?

A variety of groups is a class of groups closed under taking subgroups, homomorphic images
and (unrestricted) direct products; equivalently, it is the class of all groups satisfying
some set of laws. The varieties of groups, ordered by inclusion, form a complete lattice.
By a classical theorem (see H. Neumann, *Varieties of Groups*, Chapter 1), the map sending a
variety $\mathfrak{V}$ to the subgroup $\mathfrak{V}(F_\infty)$ of all laws of $\mathfrak{V}$
is an anti-isomorphism from the lattice of all varieties of groups onto the lattice of fully
invariant subgroups of the free group $F_\infty$ of countably infinite rank. We therefore
realise the lattice of all varieties of groups as the order dual of the lattice of fully
invariant subgroups of `FreeGroup ℕ`. This also avoids the set-theoretic issues involved in
working with classes of groups.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.27»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A subgroup `H` of a group `G` is *fully invariant* if it is mapped into itself by every
endomorphism of `G`. -/
def IsFullyInvariant (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : G →* G, H.map f ≤ H

/-- The trivial subgroup is fully invariant. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFullyInvariant_bot : IsFullyInvariant (⊥ : Subgroup G) := fun f => by
  simp

/-- The whole group is fully invariant. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFullyInvariant_top : IsFullyInvariant (⊤ : Subgroup G) := fun _ => le_top

/-- The commutator subgroup is fully invariant. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFullyInvariant_commutator : IsFullyInvariant (commutator G) := fun f => by
  rw [commutator_def, Subgroup.map_commutator]
  exact Subgroup.commutator_mono le_top le_top

/-- A fully invariant subgroup is characteristic. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFullyInvariant.characteristic {H : Subgroup G} (hH : IsFullyInvariant H) :
    H.Characteristic := by
  rw [Subgroup.characteristic_iff_map_le]
  exact fun φ => hH φ.toMonoidHom

variable (G) in
/-- The fully invariant subgroups of a group `G` form a complete sublattice of the lattice of
subgroups of `G`. -/
def fullyInvariantSubgroup : CompleteSublattice (Subgroup G) :=
  .mk' {H : Subgroup G | IsFullyInvariant H}
    (fun _s hs f => by
      rw [(Subgroup.gc_map_comap f).l_sSup]
      exact iSup₂_le fun H hH => (hs hH f).trans (le_sSup hH))
    fun _s hs f => le_sInf fun H hH => (Subgroup.map_mono (sInf_le hH)).trans (hs hH f)

/-- Membership in `fullyInvariantSubgroup G` is full invariance. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_fullyInvariantSubgroup_iff {H : Subgroup G} :
    H ∈ fullyInvariantSubgroup G ↔ IsFullyInvariant H := Iff.rfl

/-- The lattice of all varieties of groups (ordered by inclusion), realised as the order dual of
the lattice of fully invariant subgroups (ordered by inclusion) of the free group `FreeGroup ℕ`
of countably infinite rank: a variety $\mathfrak{V}$ corresponds to the fully invariant subgroup
$\mathfrak{V}(F_\infty)$ of all its laws, and $\mathfrak{U} \subseteq \mathfrak{V}$ if and only
if $\mathfrak{V}(F_\infty) \subseteq \mathfrak{U}(F_\infty)$. -/
abbrev GroupVarietyLattice : Type := (fullyInvariantSubgroup (FreeGroup ℕ))ᵒᵈ

/-- The least element of `GroupVarietyLattice` (the variety of trivial groups, whose laws form
all of `FreeGroup ℕ`) differs from its greatest element (the variety of all groups, whose only
law is trivial). -/
@[category test, AMS 6 8 20]
theorem GroupVarietyLattice.bot_ne_top : (⊥ : GroupVarietyLattice) ≠ ⊤ := by
  intro h
  have := congrArg (fun x : GroupVarietyLattice =>
    ((OrderDual.ofDual x : fullyInvariantSubgroup (FreeGroup ℕ)) : Subgroup (FreeGroup ℕ))) h
  simp at this

/--
Does the lattice of all varieties of groups possess non-trivial automorphisms?

That is, is there an automorphism of the lattice of all varieties of groups (an order-preserving
bijection whose inverse is also order-preserving, equivalently a bijection preserving all meets
and joins) which is not the identity?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 6 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.27» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ φ : GroupVarietyLattice ≃o GroupVarietyLattice, φ ≠ OrderIso.refl _ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.27»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.27

by A. V. Kuznetsov

Does the lattice of all varieties of groups possess non-trivial automorphisms?

A variety of groups is the class of all groups satisfying a given set of laws
(equivalently, by Birkhoff's theorem, a class of groups closed under subgroups,
homomorphic images and arbitrary direct products). Sending a variety
$\mathfrak{V}$ to the set of all laws of $\mathfrak{V}$, regarded as a subgroup of
the free group $F_\infty$ of countably infinite rank, is an anti-isomorphism from
the lattice of all varieties of groups (ordered by inclusion) onto the lattice of
all fully invariant subgroups of $F_\infty$ (ordered by inclusion); see
H. Neumann, *Varieties of Groups*, Chapter 1. Since a lattice and its order dual
have the same automorphisms, the question is equivalent to asking whether the
lattice of fully invariant subgroups of $F_\infty$ has an automorphism other than
the identity. We state it in this form, which avoids quantifying over a class of
groups.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
- H. Neumann, *Varieties of Groups*, Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer
  Grenzgebiete 37, Springer, 1967.
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.27»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is *fully invariant* if every endomorphism
$f \colon G \to G$ maps $H$ into itself, i.e. $f(H) \le H$. -/
def IsFullyInvariant (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : G →* G, H ≤ H.comap f

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFullyInvariant_bot : IsFullyInvariant (⊥ : Subgroup G) :=
  fun _ ↦ bot_le

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFullyInvariant_top : IsFullyInvariant (⊤ : Subgroup G) :=
  fun _ ↦ le_top

/-- A fully invariant subgroup is characteristic. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFullyInvariant.characteristic {H : Subgroup G} (hH : IsFullyInvariant H) :
    H.Characteristic :=
  Subgroup.characteristic_iff_le_comap.mpr fun ϕ ↦ hH ϕ.toMonoidHom

/-- The derived subgroup is fully invariant. Under the correspondence between fully
invariant subgroups of the free group of countably infinite rank and varieties of
groups, the derived subgroup corresponds to the variety of abelian groups. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFullyInvariant_commutator : IsFullyInvariant (commutator G) := fun f ↦
  Subgroup.map_le_iff_le_comap.mp <| by
    rw [commutator_def, Subgroup.map_commutator]
    exact Subgroup.commutator_mono le_top le_top

variable (G) in
/-- The fully invariant subgroups of a group `G` form a complete sublattice of the
lattice of all subgroups of `G`. -/
def fullyInvariantSubgroup : CompleteSublattice (Subgroup G) :=
  .mk' {H : Subgroup G | IsFullyInvariant H}
    (fun _s hs f ↦ sSup_le fun _H hH ↦ (hs hH f).trans <| Subgroup.comap_mono <| le_sSup hH)
    fun _s hs f ↦ Subgroup.map_le_iff_le_comap.mp <| le_sInf fun _H hH ↦
      Subgroup.map_le_iff_le_comap.mpr <| (sInf_le hH).trans (hs hH f)

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_fullyInvariantSubgroup_iff {H : Subgroup G} :
    H ∈ fullyInvariantSubgroup G ↔ IsFullyInvariant H :=
  Iff.rfl

/--
Does the lattice of all varieties of groups possess non-trivial automorphisms?

The lattice of all varieties of groups is anti-isomorphic to the lattice
`fullyInvariantSubgroup (FreeGroup ℕ)` of all fully invariant subgroups of the free
group of countably infinite rank, and a lattice has the same automorphisms as its
order dual. So the question asks whether there is an order automorphism of
`fullyInvariantSubgroup (FreeGroup ℕ)` that is not the identity. (An order
automorphism of a lattice automatically preserves all meets and joins, so it is the
same thing as a lattice automorphism.)
-/
@[category research open, AMS 6 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.27» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ e : fullyInvariantSubgroup (FreeGroup ℕ) ≃o fullyInvariantSubgroup (FreeGroup ℕ),
      e ≠ OrderIso.refl _ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.27»

modeling_decisions: The lattice of varieties of groups is represented by its order dual, the lattice of fully invariant subgroups of FreeGroup ℕ (the free group of countably infinite rank), via the classical anti-isomorphism 𝔙 ↦ 𝔙(F_∞) (set of laws). This follows the decomposition note's recommendation to avoid quantifying over a class of groups. Existence of a non-identity automorphism is invariant under passing to the order dual, so the proposition is unchanged. A reviewer who insists on varieties defined literally as classes of groups (in a fixed universe, via laws or S/H/P-closure) would obtain an isomorphic lattice; the equivalence relies on the standard theorem, not on any new claim.

'Automorphism of the lattice' is formalized as an order isomorphism L ≃o L; for lattices this coincides with lattice automorphisms and with complete-lattice automorphisms, since order isomorphisms preserve all existing meets and joins.
'Non-trivial' is formalized as e ≠ OrderIso.refl _, i.e. not the identity (equivalently, by OrderIso.ext, ∃ H, e H ≠ H).

Auxiliary API lemmas (⊥, ⊤ and the derived subgroup are fully invariant; fully invariant implies characteristic; membership in the sublattice) are included with proofs as basic tests of the bespoke definitions, tagged category API.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.27

by A. V. Kuznetsov

Does the lattice of all varieties of groups possess non-trivial automorphisms?

A *variety of groups* is a class of groups closed under taking subgroups, homomorphic images
and (unrestricted) direct products; by Birkhoff's theorem these are exactly the classes of
groups defined by a set of laws (identities). Ordered by inclusion, the varieties of groups form
a complete lattice, which is anti-isomorphic to the lattice of fully invariant subgroups of the
free group of countably infinite rank. An automorphism of a lattice is a bijection preserving
the order in both directions; it automatically preserves all meets and joins.

To avoid size issues, groups are taken in the universe `Type`. By Birkhoff's theorem this does
not change the lattice: every variety is determined by its laws, which are elements of the free
group `FreeGroup ℕ`, and every set of laws is realised by a group in `Type`.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.27»

/-- A *variety of groups* is a class of groups (taken in `Type`) that is closed under taking
subgroups, homomorphic images and (unrestricted) direct products. -/
@[ext]
structure GroupVariety where
  /-- The class of groups belonging to the variety. -/
  Mem : (G : Type) → [Group G] → Prop
  /-- The class is closed under taking subgroups. -/
  mem_subgroup {G : Type} [Group G] (H : Subgroup G) : Mem G → Mem H
  /-- The class is closed under taking homomorphic images. -/
  mem_of_surjective {G H : Type} [Group G] [Group H] (f : G →* H) :
    Function.Surjective f → Mem G → Mem H
  /-- The class is closed under (unrestricted) direct products. -/
  mem_pi {ι : Type} (G : ι → Type) [∀ i, Group (G i)] : (∀ i, Mem (G i)) → Mem (∀ i, G i)

namespace GroupVariety

/-- Varieties of groups are ordered by inclusion. -/
instance : PartialOrder GroupVariety where
  le V W := ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], V.Mem G → W.Mem G
  le_refl _ _ _ h := h
  le_trans _ _ _ h₁ h₂ G _ h := h₂ G (h₁ G h)
  le_antisymm V W h₁ h₂ := by
    ext G
    exact ⟨h₁ G, h₂ G⟩

@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem le_def (V W : GroupVariety) : V ≤ W ↔ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], V.Mem G → W.Mem G :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- The intersection of a set of varieties of groups is again a variety. -/
protected def sInf (S : Set GroupVariety) : GroupVariety where
  Mem G := ∀ V ∈ S, V.Mem G
  mem_subgroup H h V hV := V.mem_subgroup H (h V hV)
  mem_of_surjective f hf h V hV := V.mem_of_surjective f hf (h V hV)
  mem_pi G _ h V hV := V.mem_pi G fun i => h i V hV

instance : InfSet GroupVariety :=
  ⟨GroupVariety.sInf⟩

/-- The intersection of a set of varieties of groups is its greatest lower bound. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem isGLB_sInf (S : Set GroupVariety) : IsGLB S (sInf S) := by
  refine ⟨fun V hV G _ h => h V hV, fun W hW G _ h V hV => hW hV G h⟩

/-- Ordered by inclusion, the varieties of groups form a complete lattice; the meet of a family
of varieties is its intersection. -/
instance : CompleteLattice GroupVariety :=
  completeLatticeOfInf GroupVariety isGLB_sInf

/-- The variety of all groups. -/
def univ : GroupVariety where
  Mem _ := True
  mem_subgroup _ _ := trivial
  mem_of_surjective _ _ _ := trivial
  mem_pi _ _ _ := trivial

/-- The variety of abelian groups. -/
def abelian : GroupVariety where
  Mem G := IsMulCommutative G
  mem_subgroup H h := by
    haveI := h
    infer_instance
  mem_of_surjective f hf h :=
    ⟨⟨fun a b => by
      obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := hf a
      obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := hf b
      rw [← map_mul, ← map_mul, h.is_comm.comm]⟩⟩
  mem_pi G _ h := ⟨⟨fun a b => funext fun i => (h i).is_comm.comm (a i) (b i)⟩⟩

@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem abelian_le_univ : abelian ≤ univ := fun _ _ _ => trivial

@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem univ_eq_top : univ = ⊤ := top_unique fun _ _ _ => trivial

/-- Every variety contains the trivial group. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem mem_punit (V : GroupVariety) : V.Mem PUnit := by

/-!
# Conjecture 8.27

by A. V. Kuznetsov

Does the lattice of all varieties of groups possess non-trivial automorphisms?

A *variety of groups* is the class of all groups satisfying a given set of laws
(equivalently, by Birkhoff's theorem, a class of groups closed under subgroups,
homomorphic images and unrestricted direct products). Varieties are ordered by
inclusion and form a complete lattice. A variety is determined by the set of
all its laws, which is a fully invariant subgroup of the free group
$F_\infty = F(x_1, x_2, \dots)$ of countably infinite rank, and every fully
invariant subgroup of $F_\infty$ arises in this way. This gives an
inclusion-reversing bijection, so the lattice of all varieties of groups is
anti-isomorphic to the lattice of fully invariant subgroups of $F_\infty$
(H. Neumann, *Varieties of Groups*, Chapter 1). We use this description, which
avoids working with classes of groups: the lattice of varieties is modelled as
the fully invariant subgroups of $F_\infty$ under reverse inclusion. (A map is
an order automorphism of a lattice if and only if it is one of the dual
lattice, so the choice of order does not affect the question.)

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.27»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A subgroup $N$ of a group $G$ is *fully invariant* if $\varphi(N) \le N$ for every
endomorphism $\varphi$ of $G$. -/
def IsFullyInvariant (N : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  ∀ φ : G →* G, N.map φ ≤ N

variable (G) in
/-- The fully invariant subgroups of a group $G$ form a complete sublattice of the lattice of
all subgroups of $G$. -/
def fullyInvariantSubgroup : CompleteSublattice (Subgroup G) :=
  .mk' {N : Subgroup G | IsFullyInvariant N}
    (fun _s hs φ ↦ ((Subgroup.gc_map_comap φ).l_sSup).trans_le <|
      iSup₂_le fun _N hN ↦ (hs hN φ).trans (le_sSup hN))
    fun _s hs φ ↦ le_sInf fun _N hN ↦ (Subgroup.map_mono (sInf_le hN)).trans (hs hN φ)

/-- Membership in `fullyInvariantSubgroup G` is full invariance. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_fullyInvariantSubgroup_iff {N : Subgroup G} :
    N ∈ fullyInvariantSubgroup G ↔ IsFullyInvariant N := by
  rfl

/-- The commutator subgroup of any group is fully invariant. For $G = F_\infty$ it is the set of
laws of the variety of abelian groups. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFullyInvariant_commutator : IsFullyInvariant (commutator G) := fun φ ↦ by
  rw [commutator_def, Subgroup.map_commutator]
  exact Subgroup.commutator_mono le_top le_top

/-- The lattice of all varieties of groups, modelled as the lattice of fully invariant
subgroups of the free group $F_\infty = F(x_1, x_2, \dots)$ of countably infinite rank with the
*reverse* inclusion order: a fully invariant subgroup $N \le F_\infty$ corresponds to the variety
of all groups $G$ in which every word $w \in N$ is a law, i.e. $\varphi(w) = 1$ for every
homomorphism $\varphi \colon F_\infty \to G$, and larger sets of laws define smaller
varieties. -/
abbrev VarietyLattice : Type := (fullyInvariantSubgroup (FreeGroup ℕ))ᵒᵈ

/--
Does the lattice of all varieties of groups possess non-trivial automorphisms?

That is, is there an automorphism of the complete lattice of all varieties of groups
(an order-preserving bijection with order-preserving inverse, hence preserving all meets and
joins) other than the identity?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 6 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.27» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ f : VarietyLattice ≃o VarietyLattice, f ≠ OrderIso.refl VarietyLattice := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.27»
